summary: An Andean imperial state centered on Cusco that integrated diverse communities through administration, labor obligations, roads and regional redistribution.
currency: No widespread coined currency; state obligations were principally organized around labor.
rulers: Selected ruler: Pachakuti, conventionally c. 1438–1471; early Inca reign dates are reconstructed from later accounts.
economy: Households supplied labor taxes; agricultural production, storage and redistribution supported state projects and armies.
military: Inca rulers conquered neighboring territories from the fifteenth century, integrating extensive Andean regions.
contributions: An extensive road network and sophisticated water engineering connected and sustained communities across difficult Andean terrain.
origin: A Cusco-based kingdom began large-scale territorial expansion under Pachakuti around 1438.
decline: Epidemics and succession war weakened imperial authority before Spanish invasion, Atahualpa’s capture and execution, and the occupation of Cusco.
periodNote: 1438 marks imperial expansion; 1533 marks the conquest phase that ended the main imperial government. A successor Inca state at Vilcabamba resisted until 1572.
